hints: Count the carbons first. Notice that bromoethane has two carbons but propanoic acid has three, so stage 1 must add a carbon.
Recall which reagent replaces $\text{Br}$ with a $\text{-C}\equiv\text{N}$ group to make propanenitrile, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CN}$.
Think about how a nitrile is converted to a carboxylic acid by acidic hydrolysis with heat, and pick the pair that does both jobs cleanly.
walkthrough:
**Spot the chain extension**

Count carbons. Bromoethane is $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{Br}$ (C2) and propanoic acid is $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{COOH}$ (C3). We need to add one carbon in stage 1.

$$\text{C2 starting material} \rightarrow \text{C3 product, so add C in stage 1}$$

**Choose stage 1 to make the nitrile**

The classic way to add one carbon is nucleophilic substitution with cyanide ion to form a nitrile. Potassium cyanide provides plenty of $\text{CN}^-$.

$$\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{Br} + \text{KCN} \rightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CN} + \text{KBr}$$

**Choose stage 2 to hydrolyse the nitrile**

A nitrile hydrolysed by heating with dilute aqueous acid gives the carboxylic acid. This is the cleanest route to the free acid.

$$\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CN} + 2\text{H}_2\text{O} \xrightarrow[\text{heat}]{\text{dilute HCl}} \text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{COOH} + \text{NH}_4^+$$

**Check why the other routes fail**

Aqueous $\text{NaOH}$ on bromoethane gives ethanol (still C2), which oxidises to ethanoic acid, not propanoic acid. Ethanolic $\text{NaOH}$ gives ethene by elimination, which does not lead to propanoic acid. So only the cyanide then acid hydrolysis pair works.

options.A: Hydrogen cyanide is a weak acid and a poor source of $\text{CN}^-$ for substitution, we normally use $\text{KCN}$ or $\text{NaCN}$ in ethanol. Also, heating the nitrile with aqueous $\text{NaOH}$ would give the carboxylate salt, not the free acid directly, so this is not the most suitable pair.
options.B: Aqueous $\text{NaOH}$ converts $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{Br}$ to ethanol, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$, by substitution. Strong oxidation then gives ethanoic acid, $\text{CH}_3\text{COOH}$, which has only two carbons. This route never adds the extra carbon needed.
options.C: Ethanolic $\text{NaOH}$ causes elimination to form ethene, $\text{CH}_2=\text{CH}_2$. Oxidising ethene with acidified manganate(VII) cleaves the double bond and does not give propanoic acid. This is the elimination trap.
options.D: Potassium cyanide provides $\text{CN}^-$ for nucleophilic substitution to give propanenitrile, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CN}$, adding the third carbon. Dilute $\text{HCl}$ with heat then hydrolyses the nitrile to propanoic acid, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{COOH}$. This is the standard two-step chain extension.
